A.reason: Both provide feasible repeated comparisons, isolated inspection and evidence-based repair decisions without overclaiming meter capability. Their mounting-repair validation differs in emphasis, not primary mechanism. Candidate 1 is stronger on preparation, controlled repair, safe restoration and sustained verification.

B.reason: Candidates 0, 1 and 4 share repeated comparison plus targeted inspection and warranted repair. Candidate 2 adds source isolation through stationary measurements; 3 tests airflow excitation; 5 examines coastdown response. These conditional approaches acknowledge resource limitations and retain safe fallback inspection. Candidate 4 best fits the limited shutdown through explicit readiness checks, an inspection cutoff, reserved restoration time and clear repair and escalation decisions.

pair.reason: B4 modestly improves on A1 by making the 30-minute shutdown executable: verify repair prerequisites, prevent unintended rotation, set a restoration-based cutoff and assign unresolved operating decisions to the existing authority. These improve feasibility and safety without requiring additional diagnostic equipment.
